items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing the option of assigning community service as an alternative to suspension of students or in conjunction thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5405

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing the
option of assigning community service as an alternative to suspension
of students or in conjunction thereof

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Allows for the imposition of community service in place of or in
conjunction with suspension

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

This bill would add a new section 3214-a to the Education Law. It
would allow a school to require a pupil, as an alternative to or in
conjunction with a school suspension, to perform community service.

JUSTIFICATION:

Under the current law, school principals may impose a variety of
penalties to students who violate the Code of Conduct, including
detentions, in-school suspensions from school, and out-of-school
suspensions from school for a period of up to five (5) days.
Principals have wide discretion in making these determinations.
However, when a student commits a significant violation of the Code of
Conduct that leads to hearing before the Superintendent of Schools,
the only penalty that a Superintendent may impose, if the student is
in fact proven guilty of the violation, is a further suspension of
school. That suspension can be for additional days, weeks or months,
depending on the severity of the violation.

Under certain circumstances, it is prudent to remove students from
school in order to protect and preserve the safety and continuity of
the learning environment for other students. However, in many cases a
prolonged absence from school significantly undermines the viability
of the educational program of the suspended students. This is true
even when the students (of compulsory age) are provided an alternative
learning settings (tutoring, etc.) to which that they are entitled.
(School districts are not required to provide alternative learning
opportunities for students who are beyond compulsory age.)
Furthermore, for those students who may not be fully invested in their
schooling, a lengthy suspension from school may in fact be an
incentive to violate a school's Code of Conduct. Thus in some
circumstances, a lengthy suspension from school may be
counterproductive to the overarching goal of schools, to prepare
students to be contributing members of our communities.

It is worthy to mention that under some circumstances, school
districts can work with families to reach an agreement whereby
students must perform community service in addition to or in lieu of a
suspension from school. However, absent such an agreement, a penalty
of community cannot be imposed. Therefore, this change to the law
would provide Superintendents with the discretion to determine the
best course of action with respect to a penalty for each student who


comes before him/her after a serious violation of the district's Code
of Conduct.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.6282 of 2014 - passed Senate

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

EFFECTIVE DATE:

Immediately

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing the option of assigning community service as an alternative to suspension of students or in conjunction thereof
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5405A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing the
option of assigning community service as an alternative to suspension
of students or in conjunction thereof

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To expand the student disciplinary options by giving schools the
ability to impose a community service requirement in place of (or in
conjunction with) an out-of-school suspension

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

This bill would add a new section 3214-a to the Education Law. It
would allow a school to require a pupil, as an alternative to or in
conjunction with a school suspension, to perform community service,
with the approval of the person in parental relation. If any such
community service would be performed outside the school, it shall be
performed in accordance with a written policy adopted by the school's
board of education. The Commissioner of Education may develop model
guidelines for the imposition of community service.

 EXISTING LAW :

Section 3214(3)(b) of the Education Law authorizes a school board,
superintendent or principal to suspend a pupil for up to 5 days.

Section 3214(3)(c) of the Education Law authorizes a school
superintendent to suspend a pupil for more than 5 days.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Under the current law, school principals may impose a variety of
penalties to students who violate the Code of Conduct, including
detentions, in-school suspensions, suspensions from activities, and
out-of-school suspensions for a period of up to 5 days. Principals
have wide discretion in making these determinations. However, when a
student commits a significant violation of the Code of Conduct that
leads to a hearing before the Superintendent of Schools, the only
penalty that a Superintendent may impose is an out-of-school
suspension of more than 5 days.

Under certain circumstances, it is prudent to remove students from
school in order to protect and preserve the safety and continuity of
the learning environment for other students. However, in other cases,
an alternative disciplinary approach may be preferable.

Over the years, a number of schools have sought to impose community
service as an alternative to out-of-school suspensions. However, the
Education Department has noted in several rulings that school
districts do not have the statutory authority under Section 3214 of
the Education Law to require a student to perform community service as
part of a disciplinary measure, even if the parents and student have
agreed to such a requirement. This bill would give school districts
the explicit authority to impose such a community service requirement.

While suspensions may be justified and needed in many circumstances,
community service may be a more appropriate disciplinary option in
other cases. Importantly, community service does not detract from
classroom time, thereby ensuring that the student continues to receive
an education. A prolonged absence from school may significantly
undermine the viability of the educational program of the suspended

students. This is true even when the students are provided an
alternative learning setting as provided by law.

Furthermore, the threat of suspension can sometimes be
counterproductive. Some students do not view it as a punishment but as
a "vacation" from school. Because community service requires the
student to commit their own personal time, it is more likely to make a
greater impression on them.

In addition, community service can be a learning tool and can offer a
more constructive and productive experience for both the student and
the community. It also enables the school to fashion a more
appropriate and relevant response based on the nature of a violation.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

Similar to 5.5405 which passed the Senate in 2015, and to S.6282 which
passed the Senate in 2014.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately

summary: Relates to the imposition of community service for students in place of or in conjunction with suspension.
